messages:
olivia: quick heads-up — ran harrier13b (tokenizer v2) through an INT8 weight-only bakeoff. compared bitsandbytes (bnb) vs llm.int8. baseline fp16 looks fine but bnb shows ~1.8% drop on instrQA F1, llm.int8 shows ~0.6% drop. logs attached.

sam: can you paste the exact quant flags you used? did you enable per-channel quantization or weight-only symmetric? also batch sizes? :thinking_face:

olivia: ran with `--quantize bnb 8bit` vs `--quantize llm.int8` in our runner. config snippet:
```
model: harrier13b
quant: weight_only
backend: bnb / llm.int8
batch_size: 8
kv_cache: enabled
warmup_steps: 2
```
(no per-channel explicit override)

jordan: we saw a similar delta on code-gen slices last week. check softmax temperature sensitivity; int8 paths sometimes amplify low-prob tokens. can you share eval slice IDs?

olivia: slice ids: code-clamp-v2, instrqa-short, summarization-headlines. biggest delta on code-clamp-v2. attaching short eval table:
```
model    | fp16  | bnb   | llm.int8
harrier  | 78.9  | 77.1  | 78.3
```
(pass@1-esque metric)

mike: interesting. what's latency + mem on the same machine? bnb sometimes uses chunked matmul that trades mem for compute.

olivia: latency p50 @ bs=1: fp16 210ms, bnb 240ms, llm.int8 225ms. GPU mem: fp16 12.2GB, bnb 7.8GB, llm.int8 8.1GB.

anya: small quality delta but mem savings are attractive. ops suggestion: make a rollout with per-slice routing — if slice==code-clamp-v2 route to llm.int8 or fallback to fp16. we can do that in Console. :thumbsup:

sam: @olivia can you repro with `--warmup_steps 0` and with `--disable-prefix-cache` (kv_cache off) — sometimes cache priming changes activations under dynamic quant. also try tokenizer parity (same wheel).

olivia: will run both. also noticed bnb run had slightly different tokenization (space handling) due to python tokenizer version mismatch. re-running with same tokenizer build now.

deploy-bot: deploy:perf/harrier13b-bnb-test started by olivia at 2026-03-20T12:04:32Z :rocket:

jordan: if repro holds, add a small short-circuit eval (1k examples) into the canary job and keep canary traffic at 1% then 5% if clean. also document the slice where we force fp16.

olivia: ok pushing results in ~30m. initial hunch: bnb weight-only micro quant introduces small noise on pre-norm linear activations for code-gen. short-term plan: route code-gen -> llm.int8, keep bnb for chat and short summarization. note for docs: add tokenizer parity + warmup sensitivity caveat.
